newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks sideways, await May export data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks sideways, await May export data.

text.p: The Singapore stock market was seen drifting sideways on Wednesday as investors stayed sidelined ahead of Singapore's May non-oil export data later in the month, dealers said.

"The market lethargy is caused by a lack of confidence in Wall Street, uncertainty in the local property and electronic sectors and Hong Kong giving investors faster and better returns," said a dealer with a foreign institution.
He added that investors were uninspired by Singapore's economy, which is expected to see a rebound in the electronics sector only later in the year.
"I am neutral for Singapore," said an institutional dealer.
Some stock valuations are attractive at current levels for investors with a six to nine month outlook, dealers said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 15.43 points down at 2,014.78 on Tuesday. Wall Street firmed 60.77 points to 7,539.27.
